main_result: For symmetric B,R and j+r<=m, s_j(B+R)>=s_{j+r}(B)-s_{r+1}(R). Thus a bounded physical core with r+3 reserve singular modes at scale mu survives r arbitrarily large signed added eigenvalues plus arbitrary dense residual spectrum whose (r+1)-st singular value is <=delta<mu.

partner_result_applied.application: Partner congruence factorization with r+3 protected complementary modes gives s_{r+3}(H0)>=ell(rho)^2 mu; new reserve theorem then gives s3(H0+R)>=ell(rho)^2 mu-s_{r+1}(R).

newest_volume_result_applied.application: If the top-r spectral packet has zero footprint across a protected original-coordinate cut and s_{r+1}(R)<=a/16, then the actual cross perturbation has op norm <=a/16 and the volume theorem yields continuous density <23/a.

unresolved_implication: The bare global hypothesis s3(A)>=1 gives only three large modes and does not automatically provide the r+3 reserve required to absorb an arbitrary rank-r hostile packet. A universal proof must force a bounded physical reserve core, a protected compression/cut with small hostile footprint, or an already-paid grouped-bank/hub/ridge/pair mechanism.
next_mechanism: Use the reserve-tail inequality as a compiler inside an aggregate grouped-coordinate reduction: try to show that after extracting a small number of hostile spectral spikes, the residual matrix must either have a paid diffuse cross-volume certificate or leave enough physical reserve modes on a bounded carrier.
